frontier_question: Why did OpenAI release o3 and o4-mini in April 2025, and what did the launch signal about the direction of frontier reasoning models?

chunks.content: OpenAI released o3 and o4-mini on 2025-04-16 — the first OpenAI reasoning models with vision built into the model itself, not bolted on, and with native tool use (web search, code interpreter) trained into the model. The launch was API-first: o3 and o4-mini were available to developers from day one, and o3 was not in the ChatGPT app at launch (o4-mini was). The technique was budget forcing — a fixed maximum thought budget with task-adaptive (dynamic) compute, so harder questions think longer — and OpenAI's first private chain-of-thought policy (reasoning tokens not exposed to API callers, announced in the o3/o4-mini system card). Pricing: o3 at $10 / $40 per million tokens (input/output), o4-mini at $1.10 / $4.40. o3 set a record on the ARC-AGI benchmark — about 87.5% on ARC-AGI-1 at high compute, at or above the ~85% human baseline, the first model to reach it. With GPT-5 not yet shipping, OpenAI used the launch to defend the reasoning-model frontier against DeepSeek's R1 cost shock and Anthropic's agentic-coding push — reframing frontier capability as tool-using reasoning at commodity prices.

prior_gap_texts: OpenAI released o3 and o4-mini on April 16, 2025 [Source: ev-1].

The launch signaled a shift toward frontier reasoning models that integrate vision natively into the model architecture rather than bolting it on, while also featuring native tool use (such as web search and code interpreter) trained directly into the system [Source: ev-1].

Strategically, with GPT-5 not yet shipping, OpenAI used this release to defend its position at the reasoning-model frontier against DeepSeek's R1 cost shock and Anthropic’s push in agentic coding [Source: ev-1].

To support this direction, o3 was priced at $10 per million input tokens and $40 per million output tokens, while o4-mini was priced more accessibly at $1.10 per million input tokens and 4.40 dollars per million output tokens [Source: ev-1].

The launch also highlighted advancements in efficiency and performance through a technique called budget forcing, which uses a fixed maximum thought budget with task-adaptive compute to allow harder questions to think longer [Source: ev-1].
Additionally, it marked OpenAI’s first private chain-of-thought policy, where reasoning tokens are not exposed to API callers [Source: ev-1].

In terms of capability, o3 set a record on the ARC-AGI benchmark, achieving approximately 87.5% on ARC-AGI-1 at high compute—reaching or exceeding the ~85% human baseline for the first time among models [Source: ev-1].
